summary:
ANTRA's ninth annual dossier, reported in January 2026, attributes two of the 80 trans and travesti people killed nationwide in 2025 to the Distrito Federal. The district figure is a raw count. The inventory supplies no population denominator for the district and no general homicide rate for it, so the count cannot be converted into a per-capita rate, cannot be ranked against other Brazilian units, and cannot be measured against the district's background homicide level. It stands as two documented killings and nothing more precise.

The Distrito Federal stands under the Brazilian national framework, which the parent record carries in full. The inventory documents no district-level variation on identity documents, entry, public facilities, gender-affirming care, partner recognition, hate-crime enforcement or police and custody practice. No district court ruling, district government measure, police operation or civil-society incident report specific to the Federal District appears in the sources reviewed.
tangentialFactors: The only sub-national breakdown available is the dossier's table of killings by unit, which places the district at two deaths for 2025. No district-level data on non-lethal violence, robbery, harassment or police response accompanies it, so the district's wider safety picture for trans visitors is not documented here.
localsOnly: Resident-facing information specific to the Distrito Federal is absent from the inventory. Nothing is recorded on local policing of anti-trans violence, on access to the public health system's trans-specific services within the district, on district custody arrangements, or on municipal-level protection measures. Trans residents of the district are covered by the national legal and protection framework described in the parent record, and no district-specific gap or addition to it is sourced.
outOfScopeNotes:
The 2025 district figure of two derives from a national count compiled from reported killings, and the inventory gives no methodology note for the district line item. Whether the count is complete, whether it includes deaths of district residents occurring elsewhere, and how the district's population size compares with other units are all unresolved. A comparison against the district's general homicide rate cannot be made from these sources.

A second report on the same dossier was filed from the outlet's Distrito Federal desk but reported only the national total of at least 80 killings; it adds no district-level detail and is not treated here as evidence about the district.
